body:
## Purpose

Evaluate the maintainer-directed snekql design: application-declared Pydantic attribute contracts own value interpretation; snekql owns relational execution and result structure. Continue #593 and its isolated TypeAdapter proof without expanding into a parser-helper project.

Working direction: whole-operation no parsing / declared parsing (`strict=None`, likely default) / strict parsing (`strict=True`). Explicit validators remain active; aggregates and finer-grained overrides are deferred. No-parsing results should retain expected-contract provenance without claiming that logical validation occurred.

## Investigation

- Integers, booleans, dates/datetimes, UUIDs and JSON: driver representations, accepted inputs, successful logical values and mismatches from independent writers.
- Execute focused probes only at the already discussed public Pydantic TypeAdapter seam; source-inspect current SQLite/MariaDB driver paths and existing tests, clearly separating that evidence from native execution.
- Compare standard Pydantic types with small explicit Annotated contracts; use TDD for any research-only custom validator.
- Evaluate declaration/query readability, no-parsing result shape and typing requirements, NULL versus presence, failure handling, and remaining storage/wire responsibilities.

Research only: no production/dependency/public-interface changes, native backend suites, benchmarks, aggregate design or migration work. No merge or issue closure without instruction. The deliverable is a reviewable assessment plus isolated reproducible evidence, not an adopted redesign.
